config.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala

personas.name: Grace
personas.goals: Beat last year without burning out the volunteers
personas.hidden_agenda: Considering stepping down after this gala

personas.name: Owen
personas.hidden_agenda: His annual review depends on the gala number

personas.name: Priya
personas.hidden_agenda: Half her volunteers are the same tired people every year

personas.name: Walter
personas.goals: Nobody spends money that isn't there
personas.hidden_agenda: Remembers every gala since the nineties and will tell you

agenda.title: Tickets and venue
agenda.goal: Check ticket sales against the venue and catering numbers

agenda.title: Sponsorships
agenda.goal: Review sponsorship commitments and who to chase

agenda.title: Silent auction
agenda.goal: Confirm auction items and how bidding will work

agenda.title: Volunteers and run of show
agenda.goal: Staff the evening and agree the program

beats.summary: Sales against the catering minimum; a quiet worry about the gap
Committed vs hoped-for; Owen rounds up, Walter rounds him back down
Items and bidding; the online bidding decision
Staffing the night; Priya's number is off and nobody notices; the dance floor comes back

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Wonderful, I think we're all here. Let's start with tickets and the venue.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: In terms of tickets, we're at ninety-six sold as of this morning.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: If I may, the catering minimum is a hundred and eighty, so we're a fair way short.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: How worried should we be about that?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Honestly, not very yet. Most of the sales come in the last six weeks.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: That has been true most years. Not every year.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Just to flag, the early-bird price ended last week, so there might be a slowdown now.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: What are tickets now, after early-bird?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: A hundred and fifty each. Tables are separate.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: And the balance on the venue is due January tenth, for the minutes.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Do we have that money set aside already?

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: We do. It is sitting in the event account, untouched, as it should be.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Wonderful.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Is the venue still okay with a big crowd on the dance floor at once? Last time it got tight.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: It's two twenty capacity overall, so the room itself is fine.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: It's the dance floor I'm worried about, not the room.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: That's a run-of-show question. Let's hold it for the end.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: It'd be worth someone walking the space again before we finalize the layout.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: The last time we did a walk-through, in ninety-eight, the caterer brought a tape measure and a flask.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Walter, you've told us about the flask.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: The flask is an important part of the story. The tape measure was wrong, the flask was not.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Okay, in terms of the sales push, I'd like to send a reminder email to last year's attendees.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: When would that go out?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I'll send the reminder email to last year's attendees on Monday.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Sponsorships. Owen, where are we?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Honestly, really well. We're at about forty-five thousand committed.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: If I may, I have thirty-eight five in signed letters.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: The rest is verbal. The hardware store and the credit union both said yes on the phone.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: For the minutes, verbal is not committed.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Fair. Thirty-eight five signed, with two verbals.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: And the goal for the whole night is one twenty?

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: One hundred and twenty thousand, yes. Which is ambitious.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Last year we cleared a hundred thousand, so it's a stretch but not crazy.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Are we still offering tables at the same price as last year?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Twenty-five hundred a table. We kept it flat.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Flat is generous, with catering costs where they are.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Maybe we nudge it to three thousand for next year.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Next year is next year. For this year it stays where it is.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Who are we still waiting on, sponsor-wise?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: The bank, the dental group and the brewery. The brewery is the most likely.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Could someone get a signed letter from the hardware store and the credit union this week?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: I'll get both verbals turned into signed letters by Friday.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Thank you. I'll sleep better.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Has anyone asked the mayor's office about doing a proclamation, like the library did?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: The brewery, by the way, wants their logo on the cocktail napkins. Is that fine?

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: That's fine. Logos on napkins are fine.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: As long as they pay for the napkins.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: The silent auction. Priya, you've been collecting items.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: We have twenty-three items secured. A few more are promised.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Twenty-three is more than last year at this point, I believe.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: What's the best item so far?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The weekend at the lake cabin. People will fight over it.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Sorry, my dog is losing it at the mail carrier, give me a second.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Hello, Biscuit.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: There's a question about whether we do mobile bidding this year, on phones.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Mobile bidding costs money. The platform takes a cut.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: But people bid more on phones, honestly. They get the notifications and they get competitive.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Do we know what the cut is?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Five percent of the winning bids, plus a setup fee.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Five percent of a good auction is real money.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: And paper bid sheets mean someone has to sit there all night watching the clipboards.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Maybe we try mobile bidding for the big items only?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: That's actually what most groups do now.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: I could live with that.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Then we'll do mobile bidding for the top ten items and paper for the rest. That's what we'll do.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Lovely. I'll set up the top ten on the platform this weekend.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Just the top ten, Priya.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Just the top ten, promise.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Someone should probably double-check the cabin's insurance covers a stranger staying there.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Volunteers and the run of show. Priya?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: We have about forty volunteers signed up, which is a good start.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: That's wonderful.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: How many do we actually need on the night?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Realistically, forty-five or fifty, with check-in, the auction tables and cleanup.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Are they the same people as last year?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Mostly. Just to flag, a lot of them told me this would be their last one.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: We should think about how to recruit younger volunteers next year.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: The high school needs service hours. That's usually a good pool.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Owen, could you reach out to the high school counselor about service hours?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Honestly, I'm stretched thin until the sponsorships are done.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay, then I'll email the high school counselor myself tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Thank you, Priya. And the program for the evening?

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Speeches should be short. For the minutes, last year's speeches ran forty minutes.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: That was my fault. I'll own that.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: What if we cap speeches at fifteen minutes total, and the rest is the video?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: People love the video. The kids reading always gets them.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Then we cap the speeches at fifteen minutes and lead with the video. Agreed.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: And the dance floor? You said we'd come back to it.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: We did. Is it the space or the number of people?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The space. If we put the auction tables along the wall instead of the middle, it frees up the floor.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: That seems sensible, and it costs nothing.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: Let's look at the floor plan before we decide.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: Who is handling the raffle license this year?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Is the date still Saturday the fourteenth? I keep getting asked.

turns.speaker: Grace
turns.text: March fourteenth, yes. Nothing has moved. And I think that's everything. Thank you all.

turns.speaker: Walter
turns.text: For the minutes, meeting adjourned.
